_comment: Hand-checked corrections and first-attestation dates for the words the article leans on. Dates marked 'attested' follow the decade conventions of the Online Etymology Dictionary (etymonline.com) unless the note says otherwise. 'replace': true throws away the automatic parse for that word; otherwise the fields below are merged over it.

date.note: first attested in Thomas Browne's Religio Medici (1643); often thought to have been coined in English before it entered Latin

late 14th century, originally the Milky Way; Old French galaxie, Latin galaxias, Greek galaxias (kyklos), milky (circle)
early 14th century; Old French empire, Latin imperium
c. 1200; Old French empereor, Latin imperator
late 14th century; Old French imperial, Latin imperialis

mid 14th century; Old French rebellion, Latin rebellionem
c. 1300; Old French force, Late Latin fortia, from fortis (strong)
c. 1300; Old French planete, Late Latin planeta, Greek planetes (wanderer)
early 13th century; Old French destruire, Latin destruere
late 14th century; Old French princesse
c. 1200; Old French senat, Latin senatus, from senex (old man)
c. 1200; Old French senator, Latin senator
c. 1300; Old French aliance
late 13th century; Old French estacion, Latin stationem
